keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Drop D Blues-Metal with Syncopated Funk Groove

scalesUsed.notes: D - F - G - Ab - A - C

The foundational scale for Tom Morello's whammy-pedal octave pitch solo

scalesUsed.notes: D - E - F - G - A - B - C

mainProgression.description: Monolithic, syncopated power chord riff exploiting the one-finger Drop D barre

sectionProgressions.progression: D5 (pulsing octave stabs into open low D hammer-ons)
sectionProgressions.description: Tension-building single-note bassline escalating into the full-band drop
Iconic syncopated blues-metal riff featuring the diminished fifth (Ab) passing chromatic tone
'Some of those that work forces are the same that burn crosses' anthemic power groove
Explosive, headbanging climax repeating 'Fuck you, I won't do what you tell me'

harmonicFunction: Drop D tuning allows the low D string to vibrate with immense low-end punch while one finger barres all three bass strings (DAD)
The tritone / blue note Ab (fret 6 on low D string) creates raw, confrontational dissonant tension that resolves into G and F
Extreme use of rhythmic syncopation on offbeats gives the heavy metal riff an irresistible hip-hop / funk bounce
The song operates entirely in the dark, rebellious gravity of D minor blues

techniques.name: Drop D One-Finger Power Chords & Palm Muting
techniques.description: Barring strings 6, 5, and 4 with the index finger for thunderous heavy metal riffing

notes: Drop the low E string down one full step to D
Barre across the bottom three strings (D, A, D) with a single finger
Lock into Brad Wilk's tight snare and bass drum accents with heavy palm muting
sequence: Open low three strings (0-0-0) for massive D5 chord
Slide up to 6th fret (6-6-6) for the blue-note Ab stab
tips: Keep picking hand strictly synchronized with downstrokes on accents
Use tight palm muting between stabs to create dramatic silent space

techniques.name: DigiTech Whammy Pitch Shifting & Toggle Switch Scratching
techniques.description: Tom Morello's revolutionary guitar solo technique using a 2-octave pitch-shift pedal and killswitch stutter

notes: Set DigiTech Whammy pedal to '+2 Octaves Up' mode
Rock treadle forward to catapult single notes into screaming siren frequencies
Use pickup selector toggle switch as a killswitch (neck pickup volume on 10, bridge pickup volume on 0)
sequence: Fret notes in standard D minor pentatonic at 10th-12th frets
Toe down on Whammy pedal to sweep pitch up 2 full octaves
Rapidly flick toggle switch back and forth for rhythmic stutter effects
tips: Internalize treadle movement to hit target pitches without glancing at your feet
Maintain clean fret-hand muting so open strings don't screech unexpectedly

sections.name: Intro Build & Drop Riff
sections.description: Quiet bassline and guitar stabs building tension before exploding into the main riff drop.
notes: Start with light pick attack on the octave stabs
Slam into the full-power drop with zero hesitation

sections.name: Main Blues-Metal Riff
sections.description: The unmistakable head-nodding main riff featuring heavy palm muting and the chromatic Ab stab.
notes: Heavy downstroke attack on the low three strings
Crisp chromatic slide from 5th fret G to 6th fret Ab and back
Leave silent space between chord stabs

sections.name: Tom Morello Whammy Solo
sections.description: Morello's iconic avant-garde solo mimicking police sirens and hip-hop turntablism using a DigiTech Whammy.
notes: DigiTech Whammy set to +2 Octaves Up
Smooth treadle sweep synchronized with pick strikes
High-gain Marshall tube saturation with noise gate

sections.name: Outro Climax (Won't Do What You Tell Me)
sections.description: The furious final section repeating the rebellious mantra before the explosive final power chord ring-out.
notes: Maximum picking force and aggressive attitude
Let the low D power chord vibrate the entire room
Slam final chord on beat 1 and let feedback howl into silence

guitar.pickup: EMG 81 bridge active humbucker / EMG 85 neck

effects.reverb: Completely dry for tight, punchy percussive impact

beginner.title: Drop D Tuning & One-Finger Barre Riffs
steps: Tune low E string down a whole step to D
Practice one-finger barre chords across the bottom three strings at frets 0, 3, 5, and 6
Play the main syncopated riff slowly at 60 BPM

intermediate.title: Syncopation, Pocket & Tight Palm Muting
steps: Lock in the syncopated offbeat timing with the drum groove at 82 BPM
Master instant right-hand palm muting to eliminate unwanted string rumble
Practice the chromatic slide from G to Ab with precision

advanced.title: Whammy Pedal Solo & Outro Stamina
steps: Incorporate the DigiTech Whammy pedal with smooth foot treadle control
Practice toggle switch stutter killswitch techniques
Perform the full 5-minute arrangement with maximum physical energy and attitude

commonMistakes: Failing to mute strings cleanly, resulting in muddy low-end dissonance in Drop D
Rushing the syncopation—the groove must sit deep behind the beat
Over-complicating the fretting hand instead of utilizing simple one-finger barre shapes
practiceRoutine: 5 min: Verify Drop D tuning pitch accuracy
10 min: Slow drill of the main riff focusing on clean muting and dynamic stops
15 min: Groove practice with metronome at 82 BPM locking with the kick/snare
10 min: Whammy pedal pitch calibration and lead solo practice
focusAreas: Heavy, punchy one-finger Drop D barre technique
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 82 BPM with heavy click on 2 and 4
Count sixteenth notes (1-e-and-a) to land the syncopated hits on time
Maintain relaxed aggression without rushing the tempo
